questions.prompt: Soldiers have occasionally been trained to use the bicycle for military purposes, as described in the Wikipedia article on Bicycle infantry. questions.hint: 5 letters; heavy armored vehicles that move on tracks
questions.explanation: During the rapid Japanese advance through Malaya, bicycle infantry allowed troops to move quickly through jungle terrain. questions.explanation: La Princesse, the giant mechanical spider created by French company La Machine, weighed 37 tonnes and stood 15 metres tall as it wandered through Liverpool's streets in 2008 as part of the city's European Capital of Culture celebrations.

questions.prompt: During the infamous 1989 World Cup qualifier at the Maracanã, Chilean goalkeeper Roberto Rojas, desperate to help his team qualify for the 1990 World Cup, cut himself with a hidden razor blade to fake an injury from a flare thrown by Brazilian fans. In what minute of the match did this staged incident occur?
questions.hint: It happened sometime after the 50th minute of the match.
questions.explanation: In the 67th minute of the match, with Brazil leading 1-0, a flare was thrown near Roberto Rojas, who then used a razor blade concealed in his glove to cut his forehead, faking an injury to have the match abandoned in Chile's favor. The plot was exposed and Chile was banned from the 1994 World Cup qualifiers.
